context: Each cell in the 4×4 nonnegative integer grid gives the cost of visiting it. From the top-left start [0, 0], move one cell right or down at each step to the bottom-right destination [3, 3]. The sum includes both endpoints. Row and column indices start at 0.
description: The full 4×4 input grid on the left labels the top left “Start” and the bottom right “Destination.” An arrow points right to a copy of the grid with a seven-cell path highlighted in green from the top left to the bottom right. The caption reads, “The minimum path sum is 13, with optimal route 1→2→2→3→2→1→2.”

frames.explanation: On the right, the green optimal path starts at [0, 0] (value 1), goes down to [1, 0] (2), right to [1, 1] (2), and down to [2, 1] (3). It goes right twice through [2, 2] (2) and [2, 3] (1), then down to the destination [3, 3] (2). Its cost is 1+2+2+3+2+1+2=13.
frames.title: Minimum path sum in a four-by-four grid

summary: In a 4×4 cost grid, travel from the top left to the bottom right using only right and down moves. The seven cells on the green optimal path sum to 13.
